messages.subject: Re: [knitr] environment undefined error
messages.body_plain:
My guess is Chapter2.Rnw does not have the LaTeX preamble starting
with \documentclass{}. It is not a complete LaTeX document, so you
should not compile it on its own. Or you have to run knit() on the
main Rnw document to generate the required preamble.

Suppose this is the structure of your project:

main.Rnw
  - Chapter1.Rnw
  - Chapter2.Rnw

In main.Rnw, you should

<<chap1, child="Chapter1.Rnw">>=
@

Then knit('main.Rnw'). You do not need to knit the chapters individually.

Regards,
Yihui
--
Yihui Xie <xiey...@gmail.com>
Web: http://yihui.name

messages.subject: Sexpr conditional evaluation
messages.body_plain:
I have used knitr in the past to create a homework assignment and, based on a logical object, a homework answer key.  A minimal example is below (as it is set right now the assignment but not the answer key would be created).  This procedure worked in the past (roughly 9 months ago, I don’t know with which version of knitr) but it does not now, sending the error that object b cannot be found on line 15 (the line with the \Sexpr).  It seems that the problem is that the \Sexpr{} is always evaluated and if it returns an error then the compilation ends.  Is there a way to conditionally stop the evaluation of \Sexpr or to have the compilation not stop on errors (if there is an error in a chunk then the compilation does not stop)?  Alternatively, can someone suggest another solution?  [I imagine an inelegant solution is to have eval=TRUE always and then conditionally use echo=FALSE and results=”hide”.]

Thanks in advance for any help.

\documentclass{article}

\newif\ifdothis

\begin{document}

<<echo=FALSE>>=

dothis <- FALSE  # change to TRUE to show answer key

@

%\dothistrue    % uncomment to show answer key

The question is what is b?

<<eval=dothis, echo=dothis>>=

b <- 7

@

\ifdothis

The answer is \Sexpr{b}.

\fi

\end{document}

Dr. Derek H. Ogle

Ashland, WI  54806

messages.subject: Re: [knitr] Sexpr conditional evaluation
messages.body_plain:
Yes, I made a change in the development version of knitr a while ago:
if there is an error in \Sexpr{}, knitr will stop. In the past, the
evaluation was done in try() by default, so it will never stop. There
are two possible workarounds on my mind:

1. use try() explicitly in \Sexpr{}, e.g. \Sexpr{try(b)};

2. use a chunk hook instead of LaTeX programming, e.g.

\documentclass{article}

\begin{document}

<<echo=FALSE>>=
dothis <- FALSE  # change to TRUE to show answer key

opts_knit$set(eval.after = 'answer')
knit_hooks$set(answer = function(before, options, envir) {
  if (dothis && !before) do.call(sprintf, options$answer)
})
@

The question is what is b?

<<eval=dothis, echo=dothis, answer=list("The answer is %s.", b)>>=
b <- 7
@
\end{document}

Regards,
Yihui
--
Yihui Xie <xiey...@gmail.com>
Web: http://yihui.name

messages.subject: RE: [knitr] Sexpr conditional evaluation
messages.body_plain:
Yihui et al.,

Thanks for the help.  I did not use either of your workarounds.  I have several \Sexpr{} in my real document so I did not want to put try() in each of those.  Also, my "answers" are often more like a paragraph so the hook work-around did not seem reasonable either.  The workaround that I ended up using was to evaluate everything all of the time and then use my dothis logical to toggle whether results="markup" or results="hide".  Thus, the minimal example I sent before was modified as shown below.  The result was really only one more line of code and replacing all of my eval= with results= values.

As always, thanks for your useful and prompt help.

-----

\documentclass{article}
\newif\ifdothis

\begin{document}
<<echo=FALSE>>=
dothis <- FALSE  # change to TRUE to show answer key

doresults <- ifelse(dothis,"markup","hide")

@
%\dothistrue    % uncomment to show answer key

The question is what is b?

<<echo=dothis, results=doresults>>=

b <- 7
@

\ifdothis
The answer is \Sexpr{b}.
\fi

\end{document}

messages.subject_clean: Using source() to load functions from url (Sweave - Rnw)
messages.body_plain:
I'm trying to use a function that is available in an url. However, it seems that the function source() did not load and the pdf output did not properly work. The warning message is "could not find function corvif". However, if a read in R Console I was able to run the analysis. Is there any way for using functions in urls?

You can see below a reproducible example

#### Reproducible Example

\documentclass{article}

\usepackage[latin9]{inputenc}
\begin{document}

<<echo=FALSE>>=
options(width=60)
@

\title{Analyses from the paper X}

\author{Diogo B. Provete, Thiago Gonçalves-Souza, Michel V. Garey, Itamar A. Martins and Denise de C. Rossa-Feres}

\maketitle
This document is a supplementary material and describes all the statistical analyses we used in this paper. Please, use the Table S1.txt provided to run the code. Feel free to contact the corresponding author if you have questions or comments.
\subsubsection*{}
\maketitle
\textbf{Loading external functions}

<<LOAD FUNCTION>>=

source("http://bit.ly/dbp_corvif")

@

<<DATA&ANALYSIS>>=

dataset <- data.frame(a1=rnorm(100), a2=rnorm(100, 10, 2), a3=rnorm(20, 5))
corvif(dataset)

@

THANK YOU IN ADVANCE

messages.subject: purl() produces png/X11 warning
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

I ran purl() on a document:

> library(knitr)

> purl("cloudeqtl.Rmd")

Warning in png(tempfile()) :

  unable to open connection to X11 display ''

Note the warning that it emitted.

Questions:

1) Why that warning? Did purl() actually evaluate code? I thought it was just writing the code chunks to a .R file?

2) Does it matter? Do I need to worry that my R file is not complete somehow? Note that I don't care at this point if knit() would not work because of the X11/png() issue; I just want to know if I can trust purl() in this case.

Thanks,

Dan

messages.subject: Re: [knitr] purl() produces png/X11 warning
messages.body_plain:
It does not matter. It comes from a test of the availability of the
png() device, and it turns out that png() does not seem to be
available on your platform. From my experience, the most likely reason
is that you built R from source, but did not install the pango
headers, so R does not have full cairo support, and png() has to fall
back to X11, which is not available, either.

Regards,
Yihui
--
Yihui Xie <xiey...@gmail.com>
Web: http://yihui.name

messages.subject: xtable error going from .Rmd to pdf (via pandoc)
messages.subject_clean: xtable error going from .Rmd to pdf (via pandoc)
messages.body_plain:
I'm having some conversion issues with knitr, xtable and pandoc:

By way of example, I can knit the following chunk and convert to pdf (via Latex) with Pandoc.

```{r, echo = FALSE, results = 'asis'}
library(xtable)
print(xtable(head(iris), align = "c|ccccc"), type = 'latex')
```
But...

If I also try read in a .csv (any csv) in the same document e.g.

```{r, echo = FALSE, results = 'asis'}
library(xtable)
print(xtable(head(iris), align = "c|ccccc"), type = 'latex')
```

```{r}
myfile = read.csv(file = "myfile.csv", header = TRUE)
```

I get the following error from pandoc:

pandoc.exe: Error producing PDF from TeX source.
! Use of \@array doesn't match its definition.
\new@ifnextchar ...served@d = #1\def \reserved@a {
                                                  #2}\def \reserved@b {#3}\f...
l.79 \begin{tabular}{c|ccccc}

The problem seems like it's stemming from the vertical line in the align argument in print.xtable, but the odd thing is I can run both chunks fine independently as they are. Alternatively, all works fine if I remove the the vertical line in align = "c|ccccc" .

Any suggestions very much appreciated.
